FREE BALL 1 of 2 - THE STOPPING FIRST TOUCH NO LONGER KILLS THE BALL DEAD. WHAT CHANGES: three numbers in the trap (first-touch) placement table. When a player controls a ball and ENDS UP STATIONARY, the game plants the ball a fixed distance in front of him. This pack moves that base distance from 0.50 m to 0.80 m. WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, identically - the ball you are controlling with the stick, your AI team-mates and the CPU. This is match::anime::action::Trap, which every player runs.

EVIDENCE - a-EMULATED, and CORRECTED since the first draft of this pack. The game's own chooser 0x14405e130 was re-run under Unicorn from the PRISTINE image, sweeping BOTH flags this time (r9d, and the 5th stack-argument byte which is the BURST flag). Full outcome table for the stopping touch, in metres:
    plain path (no flags)            0.500 -> 0.800
    r9d == 2 path (+1.5 at 0x14405e343)   2.000 -> 2.300
    TRUE BURST (+2.5 at 0x14405e334)      3.000 -> 3.300
The earlier draft of this pack reported '2.000 -> 2.300' as the burst case. That was wrong: it is the r9d==2 case, and the real burst case is a metre further out, 3.000 -> 3.300. The delta this pack adds is +0.30 m in every cell, which was right; only the absolute magnitudes were understated. Read the failure-mode advice below with 3.3 m in view, because that is the case you will actually notice.

UNITS ARE METRES, PROVEN BY THE GAME ITSELF: the sibling function 0x14405cc60 prints this same value with its own format string '[trap_dist]offset=%f(m) %s' at 0x146b7bb38. That is Konami's own label, not our inference.

WHICH CODE PATH WAS MEASURED: 0x14405e130 is the shared helper, called from 30+ sites (including from all through 0x14405cc60), and it is the one emulated. Honest caveat: 0x14405cc60 ALSO contains four further inlined copies of the same three-way dispatch (0x14405d2b2, 0x14405d44d.., 0x14405d8b7.., 0x14405db9d..). Those read the raw table value with no clamp and no burst override - b-disassembly only, not emulated. The direction there is the same (a bigger number is a bigger offset), so every cell this pack raises is raised on those paths too, just without the flag arithmetic.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is a LEASH-LENGTH change: every cell is a constant picked by a discrete (gaitIn, gaitOut, flag) tuple, so this adds NO variance - a longer fixed leash is still a fixed leash. The top of the range (the 3.5 m burst literal, see freeball-carry.json) is untouched, so the overall spread narrows slightly rather than widening. No dt270 lever for per-touch variation has been found. What is DEMONSTRATED is geometry: the ball spends longer further from the foot, which gives a defender more to attack and forces more reaching, hurried contacts. What is NOT ESTABLISHED is any knock-on to the kick-error model - distance-from-foot is not among the named difficulty inputs of the kick-error builder 0x14401a900, and nothing here was shown to raise its D term. If you want more mis-hits as such, that is freeball-firsttouch.json, which IS demonstrated.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH: a hard pass into a stationary player bouncing a pace away from him instead of stopping under his sole, and pressing defenders occasionally nicking that ball. THE FAILURE MODE: receiving with your back to goal becoming impossible because the ball squirts past - most likely on a sprinting player killing a ball, where the placement is now 3.3 m rather than 3.0 m. If that happens, drop 0.8 to 0.65 (which puts the burst case back to 3.15 m). STRONGER VERSION: 1.1 in all three edits - a full stride, and close control in traffic becomes genuinely hard.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER PACKS ON DISK. This pack and freeball-carry.json are NOT a complete split of freeball-string.json. Together they are freeball-string MINUS ballForceDirect.kickBasis.offsetPos_Idle/Run/Dash and MINUS blendStartAfterFrame, and at slightly higher values (0.8/1.9 vs 0.7/1.85). kickBasis is a genuinely different trap variant with its own readers inside 0x144053700, and it stays STOCK at 0.5/1.5/2.0 after both packs - so whatever situations that variant serves still kill the ball dead. Other packs on disk that write trap.ballForceDirect fields: freeball-string.json (all 15), loose-realism-v1.json and loose-realism-v2.json (kickBasis.offsetPos_Run/Dash), duels-firsttouch.json (rateCollisionSpin). Do NOT stack this with freeball-string.json. Verified 2026-09-18 that all nine offsets and runDashSetting are live at their stock values (0.5 / 1.5 / 2.25 / 2.25), so nothing is currently applied.

NO DRY-RUN EXISTS for dt270 packs. Verification here is tools/tuning_liveness.py check (all 3 fields status 'read', 5 readers each, kind float) plus reading the live values back with gameplay_tune get. APPLY: python tools/gameplay_tune.py apply tools/data/tunings/freeball-touch.json --stack   REVERT: python tools/gameplay_tune.py restore

edits._note: 0.5 -> 0.8 m. Standing player, touch that leaves him standing. Read at [obj+0x54] by 0x14405e32b (and 4 inlined copies in 0x14405cc60).
0.5 -> 0.8 m. Running in, stopping on the touch. [obj+0x5c], read at 0x14405e2be. A runner killing a fast ball stone dead is the least realistic case in the game.

0.5 -> 0.8 m. Sprinting in, stopping on the touch. [obj+0x48], read at 0x14405e25d. All three of these cells funnel into the same tail at 0x14405e330, so all three pick up the +2.5 burst addend (0x14405e334) or the +1.5 r9d==2 addend (0x14405e343) when those flags are set.
